data.title: MVP
data.tagline: The smallest real product or experiment that tests a key product assumption
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a small experiment that produces valid evidence for a risky assumption and spot an unreliable product mislabeled as an MVP.
data.description: To test whether freelancers will pay for payment reminders, a team can charge real customers and deliver the reminders manually first. An MVP gathers decision-worthy evidence; it is not a carelessly stripped-down full product.

learning.assumes: You have seen teams cut features to ship sooner or build before testing an idea.
learning.outcome: You can choose a small experiment that produces valid evidence for a risky assumption and spot an unreliable product mislabeled as an MVP.

explanation.title: Choose one risky assumption
explanation.text: Start with the claim that would make the idea fail if it is wrong, such as whether the target user will pay.

explanation.title: Build a minimal credible experience
explanation.text: Keep only the value, participation, and feedback needed to test that claim. A landing page, manual service, or small working version can fit.

explanation.title: Set the evidence and next move
explanation.text: Decide what behavior to observe and what result means continue, change direction, or stop.

data.boundary: An MVP is not a low-quality product. It must still provide the core value credibly enough to produce evidence, including the safety, privacy, and trust the experiment requires.

lessonPractice.title: The team’s biggest risk is whether freelancers will pay for automatic payment reminders. Which MVP tests that risk first?

options.label: Sell a small paid pilot, deliver reminders manually, and track purchase, usage, and renewal
options.feedback: Correct. An actual payment directly tests willingness to pay, while manual delivery avoids building the full automation system first. Purchase, usage, and renewal behavior also show whether the value lasts.

options.label: Quickly launch an incomplete finance suite without finished data protection, then watch whether users complain
options.feedback: Poor quality and safety gaps distort feedback and harm users. Being minimal does not remove conditions required for a trustworthy experiment.

options.label: Post a free feature concept image, count likes, and treat that as proof that users will pay
options.feedback: Likes show a different kind of interest from actual payment behavior, so this evidence does not directly test the key willingness-to-pay assumption.

data.agentPrompt: Our biggest risk is whether freelancers will pay for automatic payment reminders. Design a small paid pilot that tests only that question: specify the price, refund policy, target participants, manual delivery, purchase and renewal evidence, and the result that means continue or stop. Ask for my confirmation before contacting anyone or collecting payment. Free trials, survey claims, or likes can show interest but do not count as payment evidence. Keep privacy and basic trust intact, and do not expand this into a full finance product.

references.title: What is a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?
